defaults.perspective_preference: Mutual (mNDA) is the preferred default. Amperesand's stated standard is mutual, and the executed set bears this out: mNDA is the most common type by a wide margin, followed by uNDA, with only a handful of CDAs. Draft and propose on a mutual basis; accept a one-way structure only where the counterparty is a pure recipient (e.g., investor due-diligence intake) and insists, in which case ensure Amperesand sits in the Receiving Party-protective posture.
defaults.our_role_note: Amperesand is a technology/hardware company that is most often the disclosing/innovating party (it shares product, engineering, and manufacturing information with suppliers, contract manufacturers, test labs, channel partners) but is frequently the receiving party with investors and large strategic OEMs. Because the role flips, default to mutual terms that protect Amperesand symmetrically. On Amperesand paper (the majority of the executed set) Amperesand controls drafting; on counterparty paper (investors and growth-equity funds; large OEMs and semiconductor companies; national labs/utilities) expect to negotiate against the counterparty's house form.
defaults.term_standard: Agreement term: 1 year from the Effective Date, terminable earlier by either Party on written notice. Confidentiality survival (mNDA): 2 years from the Effective Date; trade secrets protected for as long as they constitute trade secrets. uNDA survival: adopted internal default — 5 years per disclosure for ordinary Confidential Information + uncapped trade-secret tail, measured per disclosure, 3-year fallback (see uNDA_survival_recommendation). Source: mNDA 4.7 Clause 8 + 5-Opus panel.

positions.standard_position: Confidential Information should be defined broadly as any non-public information relating to the Purpose disclosed (orally, in writing, electronically, or by inspection) by or on behalf of the Disclosing Party that is marked or communicated as confidential, PLUS a catch-all sweeping in unmarked information reasonably apparent to a person familiar with the subject area as the type typically treated as confidential (or that the Receiving Party has reason to believe may be confidential) — expressly covering business/IP/operational information, derived data/analyses, shared personal data, third-party confidential information held by the Disclosing Party, and the existence/terms of the agreement and negotiations, with NO oral-to-writing confirmation deadline and NO requirement that information be marked to qualify.
positions.rationale: The confidentiality definition is the foundational scoping clause of every NDA — it determines what protection exists at all. As a technology company whose crown jewels (power-electronics IP) and commercially sensitive fundraising, customer, and supplier information are frequently shared verbally in early-stage exploratory discussions and in-person demos, Amperesand's interest is a broad, marking-independent definition that protects information regardless of whether someone remembered to stamp it "Confidential" or memorialize an oral disclosure in time. The recurring oral-to-writing reduction requirement (typically 15 days) is the single biggest practical threat: it creates an operational trap where genuinely sensitive verbal disclosures silently lose protection, and Amperesand has signed it in a significant number of executed deals. Equally, Amperesand must resist inverse failure modes: definitions narrowed to a single technology or due-diligence category (which leave most shared information unprotected), asymmetric counterparty-only expansions, and runaway-broad scope (constructive knowledge from observation/overhearing, "ordinary business" beyond the Purpose, or retroactive "before or after" capture) that expose Amperesand to inadvertent-breach claims as the Receiving Party. A subtle but real drafting defect to police is Singapore PDPA / Companies Act references bleeding into Delaware-governed US deals, which creates jurisdictional ambiguity over which privacy regime governs.

acceptable_fallbacks.position: Oral (and visual) disclosures must be reduced to writing and submitted to the Receiving Party within 15 days of disclosure to qualify as Confidential Information; written/electronic disclosures marked confidential at time of disclosure. Accept only where the catch-all otherwise survives and ideally negotiate removal first; this is the most-signed deviation despite being a recurring operational trap.

Longer or alternative oral-confirmation windows accepted on counterparty paper: 30-day written confirmation-and-marking or 14-day identify-plus-reduce-to-writing. Same operational-trap risk as the 15-day version, sometimes worse where contemporaneous identification is also required.

Marking requirement for written/electronic disclosures (must be marked 'confidential' or 'proprietary' at time of disclosure), with the reasonably-apparent catch-all preserved for unmarked information. Acceptable because the catch-all backstops missed markings.

Inclusion of the existence/terms of the agreement and negotiation status as Confidential Information, plus explicit personal-data coverage (Singapore PDPA on SG paper; GDPR for an EU counterparty). Pro-Amperesand breadth; acceptable.

Pure no-marking / constructive-knowledge definition with no oral-confirmation deadline (information protected if a reasonable person knew or should have known it was confidential). Favorable to Amperesand as discloser; acceptable on counterparty paper where balanced.

Narrowing of CI scope to a defined transaction category (e.g., 'Due Diligence Information' only) for one-shot investor/diligence contexts. Tolerable ONLY where Amperesand is essentially the recipient of investor info or the deal is genuinely single-purpose; resist when Amperesand will share its own technology.

walk_away_triggers: Definition hard-scoped to a single technology or category such that Amperesand's broader shared information — financials, strategy, personnel, customers — falls outside protection. Treat as walk-away when Amperesand is the primary discloser of IP.

Asymmetric, counterparty-only expansions of CI scope not mirrored for Amperesand: a financial investor's investment strategies and portfolio companies deemed confidential; a component supplier's samples and yield data deemed confidential regardless of marking; a large OEM's prototypes/samples auto-deemed that counterparty's CI; an affiliate asymmetry limiting Amperesand's group to an exhibit while the counterparty's group is open-ended; a single-party trade-secret call-out favoring only the counterparty.

Runaway scope beyond the Purpose or beyond formal disclosure: 'whether or not related to the project' catch-alls; 'otherwise in the course of conducting ordinary business'; constructive/inferred knowledge (catch-alls extending to information gained indirectly, e.g., by observation or overhearing) — these create inadvertent-breach exposure for Amperesand as Receiving Party.
Retroactive capture of pre-agreement disclosures with no time limit AND no post-term disclosure cutoff ('whether before or after the date hereof'), combined with broad catch-all sweeps.
A definition that limits what qualifies as protectable to a government-lab construct and anchors it to a statutory exemption, combined with a 30-day oral memorialization burden on Amperesand.

Singapore PDPA / Companies Act / Electronic Transactions Act references embedded in a Delaware-governed US-to-US agreement, creating jurisdictional ambiguity over the governing privacy regime — must be cleaned from the definition before signing.
Burden-of-proof-on-Receiving-Party language combined with an unbounded 'by its nature' catch-all that gives Amperesand no marking safe harbor as recipient.

Cloud/third-party processing acknowledgment in the definition that can be read as Amperesand accepting reduced confidentiality controls for cloud-stored CI, undercutting the non-disclosure obligation.
counsel_must_confirm: Whether to keep conceding the 15-day oral-to-writing requirement as routine: it is signed in approximately 40 or more executed deals but is repeatedly flagged high-significance PROBLEMATIC. Counsel should set a firm policy (e.g., delete it, or pair it with a fallback that oral info reasonably understood to be confidential remains protected pending reduction) rather than accepting it by default.

For investor and venture-capital counterparties, confirm the acceptable degree of one-sided/uNDA posture and asymmetric expansion of the investor's CI scope — these recur and need a deliberate firm position, not ad hoc acceptance.

Whether subject-matter-scoped or due-diligence-only definitions are ever acceptable when Amperesand is the net discloser of technology; current evidence shows them signed but flagged as materially under-protective.

Confirm the standard remediation playbook for SG-law statute references appearing in US/Delaware-governed agreements — whether to delete, replace with jurisdiction-neutral framing, or carve to the correct governing law.

Whether the 'reasonably apparent / reason to believe' catch-all (Amperesand's own template language) should be defended as standard even though reviewers repeatedly tag it PROBLEMATIC when Amperesand is the Receiving Party on counterparty paper — there is an internal inconsistency between the templates and the review flags that counsel should resolve.

Confirm position on prototypes/samples and visual/facility-tour disclosures being auto-deemed CI — given Amperesand frequently demos hardware, counsel should set a clear policy on when such auto-deeming is acceptable.

positions.standard_position: Confidential Information may be used and disclosed solely for a single, narrowly defined "Purpose" expressly stated in the recitals — for mNDAs, exploring a potential business relationship between the Parties (or a potential investment by a counterparty into Amperesand); for uNDAs, evaluating a specific service/manufacturing engagement of the Receiving Party or the Receiving Party's capabilities with respect to a defined business opportunity — and for no other purpose.
positions.rationale: The permitted-purpose clause is the operative use-restriction that converts a definition of Confidential Information into an enforceable limit: it caps how a counterparty may exploit what Amperesand discloses and provides the breach hook if information is repurposed. Amperesand's core interest as a frequent Disclosing Party is to keep the stated purpose tightly scoped, serving as the primary firewall against recipients — especially investors who also back competitors, or contract manufacturers and component suppliers who serve rivals — using disclosures for competitive analysis, reverse engineering, or an undisclosed parallel program. A Purpose that is too broad (covering "any business activities arising from the relationship," an investor-side expansion to include other investments including competitors, or disclosing-party-controlled catch-alls) effectively neuters every downstream protection. The executed set shows Amperesand reliably holds a narrow line on its own paper, so the playbook should preserve that and resist breadth on counterparty paper.

acceptable_fallbacks.position: Purpose tightly scoped to a specific named technology, project, product domain, or manufacturing/service engagement (rather than generic exploration). This is Amperesand's preferred narrowing and is broadly protective as disclosing party.
Purpose limited to evaluating a potential investment or equity investment in Amperesand (investor and VC due-diligence context). Narrow and favorable to Amperesand as disclosing party.

Generic mutual exploratory Purpose — 'exploring a potential business relationship between the Parties' — with use restricted to that Purpose. This is the template baseline and the most common executed outcome.

Purpose extends modestly beyond pure evaluation to 'evaluate and/or further/pursue' the business relationship (mutual, no investor competitive-analysis carve-out). Slightly broader than evaluation-only but accepted where mutual.
Dual investment-and-business-relationship Purpose, or 'investment and/or other business arrangements,' where mutual and investor-context. Slightly open-ended but accepted.

Minor internal-use carve-out from the Purpose (e.g., limited statistical analysis/reporting using non-identifiable portions for internal use only). Accepted as a low-significance, reciprocal expansion.

walk_away_triggers: Investor or fund 'investment management' or portfolio carve-out that expands permitted use to evaluating other investments, including competitors, using Amperesand's CI — enables competitive investment analysis and must be struck or ring-fenced.

Purpose that extends beyond evaluation to ongoing 'business activities that arise from the business relationship' once a relationship exists, permitting wide open-ended use of CI without a separate commercial agreement. Limit to evaluation only; defer operational-use rights to a definitive agreement.

Disclosing-party-controlled open-ended catch-all ('and/or other purposes only as allowed by the disclosing party') that gives the counterparty unilateral control to expand permitted use of Amperesand's information. Strike the catch-all.

Counterparty publication right over collaboration results/strategy reports with only an advance-review window and a 'reasonable request' (not consent) removal standard. Require a consent/approval gate or remove the publication right.

Executed agreement that leaves unresolved bracketed alternative Purpose language or an unfilled placeholder, creating ambiguity over the agreed scope. Do not sign until the Purpose is finalized to a single, complete definition.

Asymmetric structure on counterparty paper where Amperesand is the sole disclosing party in an evaluation framed entirely around the counterparty as evaluator, leaving Amperesand's information exposed with no reciprocal protection where mutuality was expected. Confirm uNDA posture is intended or insist on mutuality.

Anti-reverse-engineering or 'design-around' prohibition embedded in the purpose clause that is broad enough to constrain Amperesand's own legitimate independent engineering on overlapping subject matter. Narrow to genuine misappropriation of disclosed CI.
counsel_must_confirm: Whether the 'evaluate and/or further/pursue the business relationship' formulation is acceptable as a standing fallback or should be capped at evaluation-only — the evidence base is thin and it sits adjacent to the post-relationship-use red flag.

Acceptable boundaries for investor-side carve-outs: confirm that an investment-management expansion enabling competitive use of Amperesand's CI is always a walk-away, versus when a ring-fenced 'ordinary course portfolio management without use of CI' acknowledgment can be tolerated.

Standing rule that no NDA is executed with unresolved bracketed or placeholder Purpose language — recommend a pre-signature checklist control given how frequently this defect appears in the executed set.

Whether anti-reverse-engineering/design-around language and derivative-works prohibitions should be standardized as acceptable when narrowed to disclosed CI, or resisted because they may constrain Amperesand's independent development.
Treatment of the single statistical-analysis carve-out — whether it is a one-off accommodation or a fallback Amperesand will repeat.
Confirm intended posture for matters where Amperesand becomes sole disclosing party under a counterparty uNDA: whether asymmetric exposure is ever acceptable or mutuality must be demanded.

positions.standard_position: Five exclusions: prior possession; public domain (no fault); third-party receipt (no known confidentiality duty); independent development (without reference to the CI); approved-for-release by written authorization. Compelled disclosure is handled separately as Required Disclosure, not an exclusion.
positions.rationale: Carve-outs are a core protection (not boilerplate): they define the outer boundary of what the Receiving Party must protect and, critically, what Amperesand itself is free to use when Amperesand is the recipient. The two carve-outs that materially protect Amperesand's own operating freedom are independent development (so Amperesand's own R&D is not entangled with or constrained by a counterparty's overlapping CI) and prior possession (so Amperesand is not bound on information it already held). Their absence creates real IP-entanglement and litigation exposure. Public domain and clean third-party-receipt carve-outs prevent absurd liability for information that is not actually secret. The compelled-by-law dimension is structural rather than substantive: across the executed set, Amperesand's templates routinely move compelled disclosure into a standalone Required Disclosure clause (with notice, minimization, and confidential-treatment duties) and use the fifth slot for written-authorization instead. That structure is acceptable and often more protective when Amperesand is the disclosing party, but internal QC tooling repeatedly flags it as PROBLEMATIC because compelled disclosure is then not a clean definitional exclusion — counsel should treat those flags as drafting-clarity issues, not substantive losses, provided a robust Required Disclosure clause exists. The genuine red flags are missing substantive carve-outs (independent development or prior possession dropped entirely) and compelled-disclosure mechanisms that are narrower than a true notice-and-minimize regime.

acceptable_fallbacks.position: Five standard substantive carve-outs (prior possession, public domain, clean third-party receipt, independent development, and written authorization), with compelled-by-law moved to a dedicated Required Disclosure clause carrying prior-notice, minimization, and confidential-treatment duties. This is Amperesand's prevailing executed structure and is acceptable (often more protective when Amperesand is disclosing party).
Compelled-by-law retained as an express sixth (or fifth) carve-out within the exclusions list, in addition to or alongside the five standard carve-outs.

Carve-outs conditioned on written/documentary evidence (existing files, contemporaneous written records) for prior possession and/or independent development — a heightened evidentiary burden that Amperesand has accepted.

Additional counterparty-favorable carve-outs beyond the standard set (e.g., a disclosing party's own non-confidential disclosure; routine regulatory/bank-examiner examination; expiry of confidentiality period) accepted where the core five remain intact.

Prior-possession or third-party carve-out qualified by a knowledge standard ('not known/reasonably suspected to be bound by confidentiality') or a short notification deadline (e.g., 21-day notice) — minor narrowing accepted.

walk_away_triggers: Independent development carve-out entirely absent — exposes Amperesand to confidentiality/IP entanglement on its own R&D that happens to overlap a counterparty's CI. Seen and resisted across multiple counterparties in the executed set.
Prior-possession / prior-knowledge carve-out entirely absent — Amperesand could be bound on information it already held before disclosure. Observed on counterparty paper from multiple parties.

Severely truncated carve-out set (only two or three carve-outs), particularly where prior possession AND independent development are both missing. Seen on paper from certain funds and early-stage counterparties.

No compelled-disclosure mechanism at all, or one without prior-notice/minimization (information neither carved out nor covered by a Required Disclosure clause), leaving Amperesand unable to comply with a court/regulatory order without breaching.

Subjective or distorted carve-out tests that defeat legitimate exclusions — e.g., third-party receipt conditioned on 'no knowledge of Improper Action by the transferor,' or a regulatory carve-out so narrow it omits subpoenas/court orders.

Public-domain carve-out drafted as 'through Receiving Party breach only' that fails to cover information already public at the time of disclosure, or otherwise narrower than 'no fault of the Receiving Party.'
counsel_must_confirm: Whether compelled-by-law is acceptable as a separate Required Disclosure clause versus an express definitional carve-out — the QC tool flags the separate-clause structure as PROBLEMATIC, but it is Amperesand's prevailing executed practice and often more protective; counsel should confirm the Required Disclosure clause actually carries prior notice, minimization, and confidential-treatment duties before relying on it.

On counterparty paper, verify that BOTH independent development and prior possession appear as substantive carve-outs before signing — these are the carve-outs whose absence created the high-severity flags.

Acceptability of heightened evidentiary burdens (contemporaneous written records / documentary evidence) for prior possession and independent development, which narrow Amperesand's ability to invoke the carve-out.

Whether additional counterparty-specific carve-outs (regulatory-examination no-notice variants, a disclosing party's own disclosure, confidentiality-period expiry) are acceptable in the specific deal context.

Mutual vs. unilateral and US vs. SG framing: confirm carve-outs apply symmetrically in mNDAs and that Representatives are included in the prior-possession and public-domain tests where Amperesand is recipient.
Drafting-error review on notice periods in compelled-disclosure provisions (e.g., internal numeral/word contradictions in notice-period language observed on at least one counterparty's form).

positions.standard_position: The Receiving Party must hold all Confidential Information in strict confidence and not disclose it to any third party without prior written approval, use it solely for the Purpose, apply at least the same degree of care it uses for its own confidential information of like importance but in no event less than reasonable care, limit access to Representatives (directors, officers, employees, consultants, contractors, advisers, agents) on a strict need-to-know basis, remain fully and unconditionally responsible for its Representatives' breaches, not copy or record except as strictly necessary (copies remaining the Disclosing Party's property), and promptly/immediately notify the Disclosing Party of any loss or unauthorized disclosure — on a mutual basis (mNDA preferred) with no extraneous IP/use restrictions, marking-confirmation traps, or expanded-disclosee carve-outs.
positions.rationale: This clause is the operative core of the NDA: it converts the definition of Confidential Information into enforceable duties (non-disclosure, use limitation, standard of care, controlled access, vicarious liability, and breach notice). For Amperesand, an early-stage power-electronics/SiC company whose value lies in proprietary technology, the integrity of these obligations directly determines whether its disclosures to investors, OEMs, manufacturers, labs, and counterparties are actually protected. The dual standard of care ('same as own, but no less than reasonable care') and unconditional responsibility for Representatives are the load-bearing protections; erosion of either (e.g., a bare 'reasonable care' floor, or a Representative-liability release upon a separate NDA) measurably reduces Amperesand's recourse. Equally important is resisting counterparty-added obligations that masquerade as confidentiality terms but are really IP/use restrictions (reverse-engineering/design-around bans, AI-training prohibitions, broad commercial-use vetoes) or operational traps (oral-disclosure marking deadlines, prior-written-consent-to-copy, mandatory court action against Representatives, perpetual backup-data obligations) that can bind Amperesand's own legitimate engineering and business activity or strip protection for its disclosures.

acceptable_fallbacks.position: 'Representatives' expressly extended to include the Receiving Party's holding companies and related corporations (as defined in the Singapore Companies Act 1967) on a need-to-know basis. Benign template language for SG-entity paper; routinely accepted even on US/Delaware-governed deals despite mild interpretive ambiguity.

Receiving Party's responsibility for a Representative's breach ceases once that Representative enters a separate confidentiality agreement directly with the Disclosing Party (or is bound by an existing professional/legal duty). A liability carve-out; low-to-medium risk and accepted repeatedly, though it can create a coverage gap if the separate NDA is weaker.

Express prohibition on reverse engineering / decompilation / disassembly / derivative works of Confidential Information, added on counterparty paper. Goes beyond pure confidentiality into use/IP restriction; accepted in tech/manufacturing contexts but flagged where it could bind Amperesand's independent development — prefer an independent-development carve-in.

Obligation to keep confidential the existence/terms of the negotiations and the Agreement itself (beyond just the content of disclosures). Common in investment/M&A-context counterparty paper; commercially reasonable but limits Amperesand's ability to reference the relationship for fundraising/marketing.

Standard of care framed as bare 'reasonable care' / 'reasonable measures' rather than the dual 'same-as-own-but-no-less-than-reasonable' formulation. A lighter floor Amperesand has occasionally accepted; mark as a concession, not preferred.

Unilateral (one-way) obligation structure where Amperesand is the sole Disclosing Party and bears no reciprocal duties. Acceptable where Amperesand only discloses; deviates from the mutual-NDA preference and should be confirmed against the actual information flow.

Requirement that non-employee Representatives be bound by / sign a confidentiality agreement no less restrictive than the NDA before receiving CI (without the more onerous 'individually executed identical undertaking' trap). Accepted on counterparty paper as a reasonable strengthening.

walk_away_triggers: Prior written consent of the Disclosing Party required before the Receiving Party may make ANY copies of Confidential Information (impedes ordinary review/use) — resist; seen across multiple counterparty-paper deals.

Oral/visual disclosures protected only if reduced to writing and marked Confidential within a fixed deadline (e.g., 15-30 days), risking inadvertent loss of protection for Amperesand's own oral disclosures — refuse; seen on multiple counterparty forms.

Broad commercial-use or 'no use/exploitation for any commercial purposes whatsoever without written approval' restriction that exceeds the Purpose limitation and could block permitted activities — refuse; seen in certain counterparty paper.

Reverse-engineering / design-around / misappropriation use-restriction drafted broadly enough to bind Amperesand's INDEPENDENT development or test articles, with no independent-development carve-in — resist or carve out; seen in multiple counterparty forms across manufacturing and semiconductor contexts.

Expanded disclosee universe that lets the counterparty share Amperesand's CI with its investors / portfolio companies / financing sources without a direct confidentiality obligation, or a portfolio-company information-barrier gap — refuse; seen on certain fund counterparty paper where investor-class recipients and portfolio-company sharing gaps were created.

AI-training / AI-tool-development prohibition or one-sided privacy/compliance regime (e.g., cybersecurity audit rights, cybersecurity remediation at Amperesand's expense) bolted onto the confidentiality clause — refuse or reciprocate/scope-limit; seen on certain corporate and utility counterparty paper.

Perpetual or open-ended confidentiality obligation embedded in this clause, including 'indefinite' obligations for backup/archived data that contradict the agreed term — refuse; seen on certain technology counterparty paper with open-ended backup retention.

Mandatory affirmative enforcement obligation requiring the Receiving Party to take 'all reasonable measures including court proceedings' against its own Representatives at its own cost — push back; seen on certain manufacturing and equipment-supplier counterparty paper (acceptable only as vicarious liability, not mandated litigation).
Requirement that each Representative individually execute identical written undertakings before any access (operationally unworkable) — refuse; seen on certain counterparty paper.

Omission of any express need-to-know Representative disclosure carve-out, which could render Amperesand's own internal sharing a technical breach — fix before signing; seen on certain counterparty paper.
Burden of proof for any exclusion/carve-out shifted onto the Receiving Party — resist when Amperesand may be the receiving party; seen on certain distribution/component-supplier counterparty paper.
Auto-deeming all prototypes/samples/pre-production products as CI regardless of marking or context, expanding scope unpredictably — resist; seen on certain semiconductor counterparty paper.

Strict 'whichever is higher' / generally-accepted-standards care obligation or 'best endeavours to prevent breach' that imposes costly affirmative steps beyond reasonable care — scrutinize; seen on certain infrastructure and infrastructure-sector counterparty paper.
counsel_must_confirm: Whether to continue routinely accepting the Singapore Companies Act 1967 'holding companies / related corporations' Representative language in US/Delaware-governed deals, or to localize the template per governing law — it is the most frequent deviation and recurs as a flagged ambiguity.

The Representative-liability release (responsibility ceases on separate NDA): acceptable as low-risk in most signed deals, but counsel should set a guardrail that the separate NDA must be no-less-restrictive to avoid a coverage gap — certain investor and supplier counterparty deals have been flagged at high/medium significance.

Each reverse-engineering / no-derivative-works addition needs a deal-specific call: acceptable where Amperesand is the discloser, but requires an independent-development carve-in where Amperesand receives hardware/test articles (asymmetric burden flagged for multiple semiconductor and certification-body counterparties).
Acceptance of a bare 'reasonable care' standard should be treated as a concession requiring sign-off, given the small evidence count (4) versus the dominant dual-standard.
Confirm the actual direction of information flow before accepting any unilateral structure, since uNDA acceptance depends on Amperesand being the sole discloser.
Whether confidentiality-of-existence-of-negotiations obligations conflict with Amperesand's fundraising/marketing needs on a given deal — flagged for certain investor counterparty contexts.

Survival/term interactions for this clause (e.g., survival measured from Effective Date vs. termination, and indefinite backup-data obligations) should be reconciled with the term_of_confidentiality playbook entry.

positions.standard_position: The Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information (a) to its Representatives (directors, officers, employees, consultants, contractors, advisers, agents) on a need-to-know basis for the Purpose, with the Receiving Party remaining responsible for their compliance, and (b) where compelled by a valid court order or governmental/regulatory authority with jurisdiction (and, on Singapore paper, the relevant securities exchange regulator), provided that the Receiving Party (i) gives the Disclosing Party reasonable prior written notice to the extent not legally prohibited, (ii) discloses only the minimum legally required, and (iii) uses reasonable efforts to obtain confidential treatment, with prompt post-hoc notice of the full circumstances if advance notice was impossible — all such disclosure rights being mutual/symmetrical.
positions.rationale: Permitted disclosures is the operative gateway that determines who lawfully receives Amperesand's Confidential Information and under what controls — it is the practical complement to the confidentiality obligation itself. Amperesand's core interest as a frequent Disclosing Party (it holds paper on the large majority of executed NDAs, especially Singapore-origin uNDAs/mNDAs) is to keep the recipient pool tight (need-to-know Representatives only, with flow-down responsibility) and to ensure compelled disclosure is a procedurally controlled, mutual carve-out rather than an open or one-sided escape hatch. The compelled-disclosure machinery (notice, minimisation, confidential-treatment efforts, post-hoc notice) is the only mechanism that lets Amperesand intervene (e.g., seek a protective order) before its proprietary technology and commercial terms reach a court or regulator. The recurring failure mode in the signed set is asymmetry: counterparty fund and large-corporate paper repeatedly grants the counterparty unilateral rights to push Amperesand CI to affiliates, investors, suppliers, or government agencies without reciprocity or consent. Because this clause is the leakage surface for the company's crown-jewel technical and deal information, getting it right is a core (not boilerplate) protection.

acceptable_fallbacks.position: Recipient pool widened beyond employees/advisers to the Receiving Party's holding companies, related corporations or group companies on a need-to-know basis (acceptable where mutual and downstream confidentiality/responsibility attaches).

Compelled disclosure framed as a procedural permitted-disclosure clause that adds active cooperation/assistance to the Disclosing Party in resisting or narrowing the order (acceptable so long as it does not let the Disclosing Party direct the response in a way that conflicts with the order).
'Best efforts' to obtain/preserve confidential treatment instead of 'reasonable efforts' (higher burden on Receiving Party; acceptable, mildly favourable to Amperesand as Disclosing Party).
No-notice carve-out for routine/general/supervisory regulatory examinations not specifically targeting the Disclosing Party (acceptable, narrowly scoped, common for regulated counterparties).

Narrower recipient list than standard (e.g., legal counsel only, or those 'under control') — favourable to Amperesand as Disclosing Party; acceptable, though counsel should confirm it does not impair Amperesand's own diligence team where Amperesand is recipient.

Fund/investor counterparties on their own paper adding investment-process recipients (affiliated funds, limited partners, co-investors already under their own CDA with Amperesand, lenders) on a need-to-know basis with confidentiality flow-down (acceptable for investment-context deals when bounded and reciprocal in substance).
Cost of seeking confidential treatment/protective order borne by the Disclosing Party (conceded once; tolerable only as a last-resort fallback, not preferred).

walk_away_triggers: One-sided / asymmetric affiliate-, supplier-, or investor-network disclosure rights that let the counterparty push Amperesand CI to its affiliates, suppliers, or investment group without Amperesand's consent and with no reciprocal right.

Disclosure to open-ended classes of third parties such as 'prospective co-investors,' 'potential sources of financing,' or 'current and/or prospective investors' — broad leakage of CI to unidentified parties without consent.

Unilateral government/regulator pass-through letting only the counterparty disclose Amperesand CI to a government agency without notice or reciprocity, or a standing third-party inspection right not tied to actual legal compulsion.
Shifting the cost of resisting/limiting compelled disclosure onto Amperesand as Disclosing Party as a baseline term.
Requiring prior written notice to the counterparty before the Receiving Party may share with its OWN need-to-know employees/affiliates/advisers — operationally unworkable.
Fixed long advance-notice periods for compelled disclosure (e.g., 30 days) that cannot be met under urgent court/government orders, especially where accompanied by internal drafting inconsistencies.
Broad non-announcement clauses barring even acknowledgment of the existence of discussions/relationship that could constrain investor or regulatory communications.

Mandatory obligation to take 'all assistance / all steps the Disclosing Party may require' to fight compelled disclosure where this effectively cedes control of Amperesand's response to legal process to the counterparty.
counsel_must_confirm: Cost-shifting fallback (Disclosing Party bears protective-treatment cost) rests on a single signed deal and was simultaneously flagged PROBLEMATIC — confirm whether to retain as a true fallback or reclassify as walk-away.

Where Amperesand is the RECEIVING party (counterparty paper, e.g., investor diligence), narrow recipient lists such as 'legal counsel only' could hamper Amperesand's own financial/technical advisers — confirm Amperesand's recipient needs deal-by-deal.
Whether 'best efforts' vs 'reasonable efforts' for confidential treatment is acceptable to give as Receiving Party in deals where Amperesand will actually receive material CI (only 2 examples).

The active cooperation/assistance fallback is acceptable in principle but the line between permissible cooperation and ceding control of Amperesand's legal-process response to the counterparty is a judgment call — confirm acceptable wording boundary.
Group/affiliate recipient expansion is acceptable mutually but counsel should confirm reciprocity and adequate flow-down responsibility in each instance, and resist where it becomes one-sided.
SGX naming carried into US/Delaware-governed agreements is a harmless template artifact in the signed set, but confirm it should be scrubbed on US paper to avoid governing-law inconsistency.
The acceptable-fallback evidence counts here are estimates synthesized from the listed observations and are not a precise audit of all 187 executed NDAs; verify counts before publishing the playbook.

positions.standard_position: The Agreement commences on the Effective Date and expires one (1) year from the Effective Date, subject to earlier termination by either Party on written notice. Confidentiality obligations survive expiration/termination independently of the agreement term — 2 years from the Effective Date on mNDA paper, and per the adopted uNDA default (5 years per disclosure + uncapped trade-secret tail; see defaults.uNDA_survival_recommendation) on uNDA paper.
positions.rationale: The agreement term defines how long Amperesand can be bound to receive and protect a counterparty's new disclosures and the window during which breach claims can arise before the relationship cleanly lapses. Amperesand's templates intentionally use a short, fixed 1-year term so the contract auto-expires by calendar date with no administrative action required, keeping the receiving-party obligation window tight. Distinct from confidentiality survival (which can run longer), the agreement term governs the active disclosure/exchange period; longer or open-ended terms expand exposure, lock both parties in before renegotiation, and shift the burden onto Amperesand to proactively terminate. The executed set shows counterparties (especially large strategics, semiconductor firms, and investors on their own paper) routinely push to 2-3 years, and a minority impose perpetual/evergreen or floating terms that are materially worse and should be resisted or repapered.

acceptable_fallbacks.position: 2-year fixed term from Effective Date (with bilateral early-termination on written notice where available), often coupled with 30-day notice
3-year fixed term from Effective Date, generally retaining a bilateral early-termination/written-notice right (mitigates the longer default)
Early-termination on a stated notice period (7 or 30 days) rather than immediate written notice, on an otherwise 1-year term
1-year term auto-terminating early on execution of a definitive agreement re the Purpose (deal-completion trigger)
No separate agreement term where duration is set by a defined ~1-2 year confidentiality period (functionally bounded, accepted on counterparty paper)

walk_away_triggers: Perpetual/evergreen term with no fixed expiry that survives indefinitely unless a party affirmatively serves notice (resist; if accepted require a short 30-day termination-for-convenience and diary the obligation) - seen at a counterparty (flagged PROBLEMATIC), various counterparties, a counterparty (no termination right at all), a counterparty
Term of 5 years or longer (a counterparty 5yr; a counterparty 7yr minimum) - especially a counterparty's 7-year floor with NO early-termination right tied to an underlying supply agreement
Floating/open-ended term measured from 'termination of discussions' or similarly undefined event, which can never definitively expire (observed at counterparties and flagged high significance)
Unilateral termination right vested only in the disclosing party / counterparty that can cut Amperesand off mid-diligence or end the agreement at will (a counterparty - flagged PROBLEMATIC)
One-sided auto-termination tied only to Amperesand's corporate status (IPO / acquisition by a public company) and not symmetric (a counterparty trigger)

Any term clause with an internal word/numeral contradiction (the spelled-out number disagreeing with the parenthetical figure) - must be corrected before signature to avoid construction disputes (various counterparties)
3-year-or-longer term that ALSO removes the bilateral early-termination right (the standard mitigant), leaving no exit before expiry
counsel_must_confirm: Whether to set a firm ceiling on acceptable term length: evidence shows 3-year terms accepted even on Amperesand's own paper (various counterparties), so counsel should decide whether 3 years is genuinely 'acceptable' or should be pushed back to 1-2 years given many are flagged PROBLEMATIC.

How to treat the ~14 no-fixed-term/evergreen NDAs Amperesand has already signed (mostly large strategics/funds on their own paper): confirm a standing rule (e.g., require 30-day termination-for-convenience + internal diary/tickler) versus a hard refusal.
Confirm acceptability of deal-completion auto-termination triggers (definitive-agreement execution) - only 3 clear examples, thin evidence.

Confirm the survival language: templates split between mNDA (no survival clause in this section) and uNDA (full survival of all rights/obligations); counsel should confirm the intended interaction between agreement term and confidentiality survival so a short term is not misread as cutting off confidentiality protection.

Confirm position on floating 'from termination of discussions' constructs - multiple counterparties were signed despite high-risk flags; verify whether this was a deliberate concession to that counterparty or should be a firm no-go.
Confirm whether early-termination notice periods longer than 30 days should ever be accepted (none observed beyond 30 days, so this is an evidence gap).

positions.standard_position: Confidentiality obligations survive termination/expiration for 2 years from the Effective Date; trade secrets remain protected for as long as they so qualify. (mNDA Clause 8 sets this 2-year standard. The uNDA Clause 8 sets no period — a drafting defect — for which the adopted internal default is the 5-Opus panel recommendation in defaults.uNDA_survival_recommendation: 5 years per disclosure for ordinary Confidential Information + an uncapped trade-secret tail, measured from each disclosure, with a 3-year pre-authorized fallback; pending counsel refinement.)
positions.rationale: As an early-stage power-electronics company, Amperesand is overwhelmingly the disclosing party of sensitive technical, manufacturing, and financing information, so the survival tail is the single most important driver of how long that information is actually protected. The standard Clause 8 measures the survival period from the Effective Date rather than from termination or expiration, which has a structural consequence worth understanding: it compresses the post-expiry protection tail by up to a full agreement term — for example, on a 1-year agreement, the 2-year-from-Effective-Date standard yields only roughly 1 year of post-expiry protection, and where the agreement term equals the survival figure the effective post-expiry tail is zero. The mirror-image risk is over-long or perpetual survival on counterparty paper — 5-year terms, perpetual backup-copy carve-outs, and open-ended 'qualifies as confidential under applicable law' tails — that burden Amperesand whenever it is the receiving party. Getting both the duration and the anchor point right is core to the NDA's purpose, which is why this is a core-protection clause rather than boilerplate.

acceptable_fallbacks.position: 3 years measured from the Effective Date — the most common executed-deal deviation above the 2-year template standard (effective post-expiry tail is roughly 2 years on a 1-year agreement term). Acceptable and slightly more protective than the standard; where a longer tail is wanted the preferred fix is to re-anchor to termination or expiration.

3 years from the date of disclosure of each item of Confidential Information (rolling per-item clock; matches the 3-year duration and is often more protective for late disclosures). Clean, acceptable formulation.
3 years from the date of termination or expiration (Amperesand's ideal anchor point; observed but rare in the executed set).

2 years post-term measured from termination or expiry — the 2-year standard re-anchored to termination, which is more protective than the 2-year-from-Effective-Date template default; commonly seen and preferred where counsel wants the fuller tail. (Weaker variants measure the 2 years from the Effective Date, matching the template standard.)
5 years post-term or 5 years from disclosure (longer survival accepted on large-counterparty paper where Amperesand is often the recipient; tolerable but extends Amperesand's own compliance burden).

Perpetual or indefinite survival arising from a cross-reference defect in Amperesand's own uNDA Clause 4/Clause 8 (no fixed sunset). Tolerated when Amperesand is the disclosing party on its own paper, but carries enforceability risk and should not be exported to deals where Amperesand may be the recipient. (The adopted go-forward fix for this defect is the per-disclosure default in defaults.uNDA_survival_recommendation: 5 years per disclosure + uncapped trade-secret tail, 3-year fallback.)
Perpetual trade-secret carve-out layered on a finite (2–3 year) general survival period — consistent with Amperesand's own template intent and market practice.

walk_away_triggers: No post-termination survival at all, or confidentiality co-terminous with the agreement term, leaving disclosed information unprotected once a (potentially very short) term ends or definitive documents are signed — seen across multiple investor, fund, and manufacturing counterparties.

Survival measured from the Effective Date where the survival figure equals or is shorter than the agreement term, producing zero or near-zero effective post-expiry protection — for example, a 3-year survival period from Effective Date on a 3-year agreement term produces no tail whatsoever.
1-year (or shorter) rolling per-disclosure survival when Amperesand is the sole or primary discloser and no trade-secret carve-out is included.

2-year survival measured from the Effective Date on a 1-year agreement term (effective approximately 1-year tail) with no trade-secret carve-out — resist; insist on at minimum a trade-secret carve-out and re-anchoring to termination.

Perpetual or indefinite survival imposed on Amperesand when Amperesand is the RECEIVING party — including open-ended 'qualifies as confidential under applicable law' tails and perpetual retained-copy or backup carve-outs seen on large-counterparty paper.
Internally contradictory or ambiguous survival drafting that a court could read either as expiring with the agreement or as perpetual — must be fixed to a clear finite period before signing.
Drafting-error figures (e.g., a spelled-out number disagreeing with its parenthetical figure) that create construction-dispute risk — must be corrected before execution.
counsel_must_confirm: RESOLVED (2026-06-18 reconciliation): canonical confidentiality survival = 2 years from the Effective Date for ordinary Confidential Information + trade secrets protected for as long as they qualify (mNDA Clause 8). Forward-looking: counsel may amend templates to re-anchor survival to termination/expiration or per-disclosure for a fuller tail.

FORWARD-LOOKING POLICY: decide whether to globally redraft templates to anchor survival to termination/expiration (or per-disclosure) rather than the Effective Date. The 2-year-from-Effective-Date standard is confirmed template-true; this is an optional improvement, not a defect fix.

ADOPTED (pending counsel): the uNDA Clause 4/Clause 8 cross-reference set no sunset. Adopted default per the 5-Opus panel: 5yr per-disclosure ordinary CI + uncapped trade-secret tail, 3yr fallback (see defaults.uNDA_survival_recommendation and PLAYBOOK_v3_RECONCILIATION.md). Counsel to confirm and redraft.

ADOPTED (pending counsel): perpetual/uncapped trade-secret carve-out is the standard default across both entity papers; counsel to confirm and supply approved language (note it is absent from the uNDA Service Provider variant and several executed deals).
STANDING (counsel): confirm jurisdiction-specific survival and data-protection handling for each entity (US Inc. vs SG Pte Ltd; SG paper raises personal-data perpetual obligations).

STANDING (per-deal judgment): set the maximum acceptable survival when Amperesand is the receiving party, given 5-year and perpetual retained-copy obligations from large counterparties have been signed.

positions.standard_position: On the Disclosing Party's written request or upon expiration/termination of the Agreement, the Receiving Party must, within fourteen (14) days, return or destroy (at the Receiving Party's election) all Confidential Information and copies, except that it may retain one (1) archival copy (including electronic records generated by automatic archiving/back-up) solely to perform surviving obligations and as required by law, court order, regulatory authority, or internal audit/compliance procedures, with the Agreement continuing to apply to any retained copy.
positions.rationale: Return/destruction is the operational backstop that limits how long a counterparty can hold Amperesand's Confidential Information after a deal dies. Amperesand's templates are highly consistent across all 8 variants (mutual/unilateral, US/SG, company/individual): a 14-day deadline triggered by either written request or expiry/termination, return-or-destroy at the Receiving Party's election, and a single archival-copy carve-out tied to surviving obligations plus legal/regulatory/audit/compliance retention, with the Agreement continuing to govern the retained copy. The clause matters because the value of every other confidentiality protection erodes if a counterparty can retain copies indefinitely or under self-defined internal policies. The dominant practical risk is not the timeline (well-accepted) but retention-scope creep: backup/archival carve-outs with no sunset, internal document-retention-policy carve-outs that let the counterparty keep CI for as long as its own policies allow, derivative work-product carve-outs, and conversion of the obligation from return-or-destroy on request into retain per internal policy. On its own paper Amperesand consistently lands its standard. The deviations worth resisting almost all appear on counterparty paper and turn the duty into an illusory one.

acceptable_fallbacks.position: Single retained copy carve-out expressly extended to 'internal audit or internal compliance procedures' and/or automatic archiving/back-up copies (beyond pure legal/regulatory hold), with the retained copy remaining subject to the Agreement. This is the most common observed variation and aligns with Amperesand's own template language.
Longer return/destruction window of 30 days (rather than 14) triggered by written request or termination/expiration, archival/legal-hold carve-out preserved.
Shorter/tighter return window of 7-15 days on counterparty paper, with standard backup/legal carve-outs.
Retention of automatic IT backup/disaster-recovery copies conditioned on no ordinary-course access and continuing confidentiality obligations (copies destroyed only on normal expiry of backup cycle).

Written certification of destruction (including officer/executive certification, or certification at Disclosing Party's option) added as a procedural requirement — accepted as a mild added burden, often net-protective to Amperesand as discloser.
Retention of one archival copy solely for dispute-resolution/determining scope of obligations (a narrowed compliance carve-out), retained copy bound by Agreement.

walk_away_triggers: Retention satisfied by reference to the Receiving Party's own record-retention schedule or internal document-retention/governance policy, allowing the counterparty to keep Amperesand CI for as long as its policies permit — this renders the destroy obligation illusory.

Open-ended/indefinite retention of automatic backup or archival copies with no sunset and a perpetual confidentiality tail, especially where it effectively negates return/destruction of all electronically stored information.

Broad carve-out permitting retention of derivative work product — notes, summaries, memoranda, analyses, business records — so that materials derived from Amperesand CI need not be returned or destroyed.

Blanket right for a counterparty's professional advisors (attorneys, accountants, brokers, financial institutions) to retain copies per their own practice, untethered from a specific legal requirement.
Unilateral legal-department retention carve-out permitting indefinite retention for 'litigation, regulatory compliance, or corporate record-keeping' without Disclosing Party consent.
Asymmetric/non-reciprocal retention rights in a mutual or investor context (retention privileges granted only to the counterparty/investor and not to Amperesand).
A requirement that Amperesand affirmatively hand over to a counterparty all work product it derived from that counterparty's information (beyond return/destroy).
Return-only obligation with no destruction option and no certification mechanism, forcing physical return of all electronically stored CI.
Loss of any trigger for return on demand — e.g., obligation arises only on a 'decision not to invest/proceed' with no right for Amperesand to demand return at any time or on expiry.
counsel_must_confirm: Whether to accept certification-of-destruction obligations on Amperesand-paper deals as standard going forward — reviewers consistently treated certification as net-protective when Amperesand is discloser but as a 'minor gap' when absent; counsel should decide whether to add a certification-on-request right to the templates.

The acceptable outer bound on return-window length when counterparties push past 14 days — 30-day windows were repeatedly signed, and isolated 90-day windows were accepted; counsel should set a hard cap (recommend 30 days) below which no escalation is needed.

Whether 'internal audit/internal compliance procedures' retention language (present in Amperesand's own templates and the most common deviation) should be tightened to require the retained copy be inaccessible in the ordinary course and subject to a defined deletion trigger, given multiple medium-flagged entries note it could permit de facto indefinite retention.

Treatment of several high-severity/PROBLEMATIC entries involving broad or policy-based indefinite retention by large counterparties — confirm these were one-off concessions to high-leverage counterparties and should not be coded as acceptable fallbacks; document any business rationale.

Whether perpetual confidentiality tails on retained backup copies are acceptable given Amperesand's general confidentiality term, or whether retention obligations should sunset with the Agreement's confidentiality period.

Investor/VC and large-enterprise counterparties systematically demand internal-policy/backup retention carve-outs; counsel should pre-clear a standard fallback rider (no-access, dispute-only use, continuing confidentiality) to deploy rather than negotiating ad hoc.

positions.standard_position: Amperesand's templates contain no residuals clause and no competitive-use carve-out; the recipient must keep Confidential Information confidential and use it solely for the defined Purpose, with no right to use memory-retained "residuals" or to apply Confidential Information to evaluate, develop, or invest in competing products or companies.
positions.rationale: Residuals and competitive-use carve-outs are the single most damaging clause type for Amperesand as a disclosing party. As an early-stage company sharing technical and commercial Confidential Information with investors and research counterparties, a broad residuals clause lets the recipient freely use memory-retained ideas, know-how, and techniques for any purpose, and competitive-use carve-outs expressly authorize the recipient to evaluate, fund, or build competitors using Amperesand's information. These provisions are practically impossible to police — memory-based use leaves no trail — and gut the protective value of the NDA precisely where the disclosure risk is highest. The executed set shows Amperesand has repeatedly signed these provisions on counterparty paper from investor counterparties, which is a pattern of accepted risk that should be actively resisted going forward.

acceptable_fallbacks.position: Soft/qualified residuals limited to employee reassignment, expressly prohibiting direct use of Confidential Information (no general memory-use carve-out). This is the narrowest residuals-type concession observed and the only one approaching acceptability, though memory-based use remains hard to police.

walk_away_triggers: Broad residuals clause permitting use of information retained in the unaided memory of representatives for any purpose (e.g., a clause permitting residual information to be used in the ordinary course of a counterparty's business).

Competitive-use or investment-management carve-out expressly permitting a counterparty to use Amperesand's Confidential Information to evaluate, fund, or invest in companies competitive with Amperesand.

Provision allowing a counterparty's affiliates, incubation programs, or portfolio companies to develop information similar to Amperesand's Confidential Information with no obligation to disclose or restrict.
Non-restriction or anti-exclusivity clause leaving a counterparty free to evaluate, acquire, or independently develop competing technologies or products without a written agreement.
Any residuals or employee-reassignment clause lacking an express prohibition on direct use of Confidential Information.
counsel_must_confirm: Confirm the actual template default and whether mutual/unilateral or US/SG variants treat residuals differently before finalizing the standard position, as no standard-position template text was supplied to the synthesis.

The only near-acceptable fallback (a qualified employee-reassignment clause from a single counterparty) rests on one document — counsel should decide whether to codify it as acceptable or hold the line at zero residuals.

Some observed provisions are arguably non-restriction or anti-exclusivity terms rather than classic residuals clauses; confirm whether the playbook should treat these under 'residuals' or split into a separate competitive-use/non-restriction entry.

For unavoidable investor counterparties demanding residuals, confirm acceptable mitigations (e.g., narrowing to genuinely incidental memory, excluding trade secrets, source code, and roadmap information, capping to non-deliberate retention, and barring use to compete) for negotiation.

positions.standard_position: The Disclosing Party retains all right, title and interest in its Confidential Information (including all copies and extracts) and grants no licenses or rights of any kind except as expressly set forth in the Agreement, and nothing in the Agreement grants any license to, or waiver of, any patents, copyrights, trademarks, or mask works (express, implied, by estoppel, or otherwise).
positions.rationale: This is a core defensive protection that prevents disclosure during diligence or commercial discussions from being construed as an implied license or transfer of Amperesand's IP. It is cheap to obtain, near-universally accepted, and uncontroversial: the overwhelming majority of the executed NDAs match Amperesand's standard verbatim or in substance. The position is uniform across all eight templates (US/SG, mutual/unilateral, company/individual) and across counterparty paper, so there is no US/SG or mutual/unilateral divergence to reconcile on the no-license core itself; the individual/uNDA variants simply add adjacent no-obligation-to-disclose and no-obligation-to-transact language that does not change the IP reservation. The real playbook risk sits in the opposite direction: a recurring block of Amperesand-paper unilateral NDAs bolts a sweeping forward-looking IP assignment/vesting clause onto the no-license provision, capturing any IP the Receiving Party creates "in the course of interaction" or "directly or indirectly" from the Information. While facially favorable to Amperesand as discloser, counsel flagged these as overreaching, likely partially unenforceable, deal-deterring, and a precedent-contamination risk if cited as Amperesand's "standard." More acutely, when the same assignment-on-derivatives concept appears on counterparty paper in a mutual NDA, it flips against Amperesand and can compel Amperesand to assign IP it develops that merely touches counterparty information.

acceptable_fallbacks.position: Functionally equivalent no-license/no-IP-grant wording on counterparty paper (e.g., 'CI remains Discloser's property; no rights or license granted or implied') with no enumerated patent/copyright/trademark/mask-work list — accept as substantively meeting Amperesand's standard.

No-license core plus a minor protective add-on running on Amperesand (no removal of proprietary legends / add legends on request; reverse-engineering or decompilation bar; warranty that discloser has the right to disclose) — accepted as immaterial.
Broad freedom-to-compete / no-restriction-on-portfolio-companies language appended to the no-license clause on investor paper — counterparty-favorable but accepted in investment-context deals.
No express no-license clause present; reliance on general ownership-reservation/purpose-limitation language or default law — acceptable only in short-form or counterparty-paper NDAs, not preferred.

walk_away_triggers: Any IP assignment, vesting, or work-for-hire obligation on counterparty paper that requires Amperesand (as Recipient) to assign or transfer ownership of IP, inventions, or 'derivatives of Confidential Information' it creates — such obligations have been observed in counterparty paper from large industrial and manufacturing counterparties; strike or carve out Amperesand's pre-existing and independently developed IP.
A patent-filing prohibition or any clause barring Amperesand from filing patent applications relating to information it receives, where Amperesand is the recipient — resist or narrow.

'Derived directly or indirectly' or 'in the course of interaction' IP-capture language in any mutual NDA, which can sweep in Amperesand's own innovations that merely touch counterparty information; require a clear carve-out for pre-existing, independently developed, and residual-knowledge IP.
Any provision purporting to grant the Receiving Party an affirmative license to Amperesand's IP, or to deem disclosure an implied license or waiver of patent/copyright/trademark/mask-work rights.
counsel_must_confirm: On Amperesand's OWN unilateral paper, decide whether to retain the sweeping IP-assignment/vesting language present in some template variants: although a meaningful number of counterparties signed it, every instance was flagged high/PROBLEMATIC for enforceability (especially in Asian, SG, and EU jurisdictions), counterparty deterrence, and precedent-contamination risk if cited as Amperesand's standard. Counsel should confirm whether to remove it from the NDA and move IP assignment to a separate services or development agreement, or at minimum add carve-outs for pre-existing and independently developed IP.

Confirm acceptability of omitting an express no-license clause in short-form or counterparty-paper deals (relying on default law and ownership reservation) — this has been treated as medium-significance in some executed deals, suggesting it should be a case-by-case legal call rather than an automatic accept.

Confirm treatment of one-sided CI-scope expansions bundled with no-license provisions (such as provisions that auto-deem prototypes or samples as confidential) that lack an Amperesand equivalent in a mutual NDA — rated medium significance where the asymmetry is unreciprocated.
Confirm position on broad freedom-to-compete/portfolio-company carve-outs added by investor counterparties on their own paper, where Amperesand's standard form is silent on the matter.

positions.standard_position: Confidential Information is provided "AS IS" with the Disclosing Party (and its Representatives) making no representation or warranty, express or implied, as to its accuracy, completeness, or fitness for any purpose and bearing no liability for the Receiving Party's use of or reliance on it; the Disclosing Party is under no obligation to supply any particular Confidential Information, and neither Party is obligated to enter into any transaction (with no partnership, joint venture, or agency created), with each Party free to terminate discussions at any time.
positions.rationale: The no-warranty/no-obligation clause is the principal liability shield in an NDA: it ensures that sharing technical and commercial information during diligence does not expose Amperesand to claims about the quality, accuracy, or completeness of what it disclosed, and confirms no deal obligation arises merely from talking. As a company that both discloses sensitive technical data and receives counterparty material, Amperesand benefits from a mutual "AS IS" disclaimer. The provision is structurally protective and substantially uncontested in the market, but two patterns require attention: (1) where Amperesand is the receiving party, the disclaimer reduces any recourse it has if counterparty information is wrong, which is an accepted trade-off in an NDA; and (2) the clause can become a vehicle for a counterparty to smuggle in broader limitation-of-liability or consequential-damages waivers that cap Amperesand's recovery against a counterparty that misuses Amperesand's CI. The default is highly favorable and near-universal, so the risk lies not in the disclaimer itself but in over-broad add-ons and in the rare total absence of the clause.

acceptable_fallbacks.position: Disclosing Party gives a narrow affirmative warranty only that it has the right/authority to disclose the Confidential Information, with all other warranties disclaimed and CI provided AS IS.
No-warranty disclaimer expressly extended to the Disclosing Party's Representatives (shareholders, officers, directors, employees, agents, advisors), with no liability on any of them for use of CI.

Broader express disclaimer adding fitness-for-purpose, merchantability, title, non-infringement, sufficiency, and/or performance, plus a Disclosing-Party damages exclusion for the Receiving Party's use of CI.
Disclaimer expressly confirming no obligation to disclose, to commence/continue negotiations, or to enter into any further agreement, with each Party bearing its own costs.

Disclaimer that expressly negates any Disclosing-Party indemnification of the Receiving Party against third-party claims arising from disclosed information (acceptable because mutual and Amperesand is also a discloser).

walk_away_triggers: A consequential/indirect/special/punitive damages waiver or any limitation-of-liability cap bundled into the no-warranty clause that would limit Amperesand's recovery (including lost profits and attorneys' fees) when a counterparty misuses or improperly discloses Amperesand's Confidential Information — resist; if it must remain, carve out breaches of confidentiality and misappropriation of IP from the damages waiver.
Outright deletion of any no-warranty/AS-IS disclaimer, leaving Amperesand exposed to accuracy/completeness/quality claims about the information it shares — require the disclaimer to be reinstated.
A one-directional damages exclusion or non-reliance limitation that protects only the counterparty as discloser while leaving Amperesand fully liable as discloser — require mutuality.

Any affirmative warranty by Amperesand beyond the narrow right-to-disclose (e.g., warranting accuracy, completeness, non-infringement, fitness, or performance of Amperesand's Confidential Information) — refuse.
A no-warranty clause coupled with an indemnity obligation on Amperesand for the counterparty's use of or reliance on the disclosed information — refuse (indemnity in an NDA is dealbreaker-class).

positions.standard_position: Each Party acknowledges that monetary damages alone may be insufficient for a breach and agrees that the Disclosing Party (or, in a mutual NDA, either Party as Disclosing Party) is entitled to seek specific performance or injunctive relief from any court in any jurisdiction, as a non-exclusive remedy in addition to all other remedies available at law or in equity, with no requirement to post a bond and no waiver of, or cap on, monetary damages.
positions.rationale: This is Amperesand's enforcement backstop. Confidential technical IP cannot be un-disclosed, so the ability to obtain a fast, court-ordered injunction (including from a court outside the SIAC/AAA/ICC arbitration seat) is the only remedy that actually protects the trade secret before damage spreads. The "any court in any jurisdiction" language deliberately carves equitable/interim relief out of the mandatory arbitration clause so Amperesand can move quickly in the jurisdiction where misuse is happening, and the cumulative/non-exclusive framing preserves the full damages claim alongside it. Because Amperesand is overwhelmingly the disclosing party in its unilateral NDAs, anything that weakens injunctive access, caps damages, or pre-commits Amperesand (in a Recipient role) to not opposing an injunction directly erodes its core protection.

acceptable_fallbacks.position: Injunctive relief / specific performance from a 'court of competent jurisdiction' rather than 'any court in any jurisdiction' (interim-relief carve-out from arbitration preserved, but forum slightly narrowed).
Injunctive relief without any requirement to post a bond or furnish security (express no-bond language added).
One-sided injunctive right running only to the Disclosing Party in a unilateral NDA where Amperesand is the sole discloser (acceptable because Amperesand holds the enforcement tool).

Recipient pre-consents / agrees not to oppose injunctive relief on adequacy-of-remedy grounds (acceptable as counterparty paper where Amperesand is primarily discloser, but flag if Amperesand can be a Recipient).
Mutual exclusion of special/indirect/consequential/punitive damages alongside preserved injunctive relief (damages limitation not in Amperesand baseline; accepted but increases exposure-limit risk).
Added obligation on Receiving Party to actively restrain its Representatives (including via court proceedings) / proactively notify Discloser of breach.

walk_away_triggers: Recipient must waive all rights to oppose the granting of injunctive/equitable relief sought by the Disclosing Party (blanket pre-emptive waiver of Amperesand's litigation/defense rights when Amperesand is in a Recipient role) — refuse any such pre-emptive waiver.
A low or fixed bond cap (e.g. a specific nominal dollar ceiling such as USD 10,000) that a court could read as limiting the relief or security available — refuse any numeric bond cap.
Prevailing-party attorneys'-fee shifting tied to remedies/enforcement, which asymmetrically deters Amperesand from enforcing — resist.
Broad mutual waiver of consequential/special/punitive/exemplary damages with only narrow carve-outs, materially capping Amperesand's recovery for misuse of IP.
Injunctive relief narrowed to IP-rights infringement only, excluding ordinary confidentiality breaches.
Complete omission of any injunctive-relief/irreparable-harm clause, leaving Amperesand without express equitable-remedy acknowledgment.
Injunctive/no-oppose right made one-sided in the counterparty's favour, or against Amperesand, in a mutual NDA.
Indemnification or uncapped damages liability bundled into the remedies clause beyond standard NDA scope.
counsel_must_confirm: Whether to accept express no-oppose / pre-consent-to-injunction language when Amperesand could itself be a Recipient (mutual NDAs): tolerable when Amperesand is sole discloser, but in mNDAs it waives Amperesand's defense rights — confirm acceptable per deal.

Bond posture: confirm Amperesand prefers an explicit no-bond clause and will reject any numeric bond cap; confirm whether silence on bond is acceptable under the governing law (US vs Singapore differ on bond requirements).

Damages-limitation interaction: standard NDA template carries no consequential-damages waiver; counsel must decide deal-by-deal whether to accept a mutual waiver (seen accepted in a small number of deals) given it caps Amperesand's recovery for IP misuse.

Arbitration/forum coordination: 'any court in any jurisdiction' alongside SIAC/AAA/ICC clauses with no express carve-out wording has been flagged in multiple executed deals — confirm a clean interim-relief carve-out is drafted so the broad forum language is not challenged as inconsistent with mandatory arbitration.
Attorneys'-fee shifting: confirm Amperesand's blanket position to reject prevailing-party fee provisions in NDAs (only one observed acceptance, flagged PROBLEMATIC).
Whether to actively resist a low bond-cap precedent retroactively or treat each instance as a one-off — needs a firm playbook rule from counsel.

positions.standard_position: On Amperesand's own paper, the Agreement is governed by Singapore law with SIAC arbitration (prevailing rules, seat Singapore, single arbitrator, English) for the SG-entity templates, and by Delaware law with AAA arbitration (Commercial Arbitration Rules, single arbitrator, seat in Nevada, USA) for the US-entity templates.
positions.rationale: Governing law and dispute resolution determine which legal regime interprets Amperesand's confidentiality obligations and where/how it enforces them. Amperesand's home positions (Singapore+SIAC; Delaware+AAA) keep disputes in familiar, arbitration-based forums offering confidentiality, cross-border enforceability under the New York Convention, and predictable corporate-law interpretation. Drifting to a counterparty's home jurisdiction (the frequent outcome on counterparty paper) imposes unfamiliar substantive law, home-court advantage for the other side, higher cost, and sometimes loss of arbitration privacy via court litigation. This is a high-volume, heavily negotiated clause; consistency protects enforceability of every other NDA term. It is important but not dealbreaker-class on its own, since most governing-law concessions are survivable provided a clear, enforceable forum exists.

acceptable_fallbacks.position: Singapore governing law with dispute resolution in Singapore COURTS (exclusive jurisdiction) instead of SIAC arbitration; home law retained, arbitration privacy/enforceability benefits lost.
Delaware governing law (US standard) with dispute resolution in Delaware COURTS instead of AAA arbitration.

Delaware governing law with AAA arbitration SEAT set to Delaware (rather than the template's Nevada seat) — the most common US-paper seat drift, typically to align the seat with the governing law; low substantive risk, both US.
New York governing law (typically NY courts, no arbitration) as a neutral US substitute for Delaware; counterparty home-state preference.
California governing law (counterparty home-state), generally with California courts and no arbitration.
Massachusetts governing law / Massachusetts courts (counterparty home-state) substituted for Delaware.

SG paper (Singapore law + SIAC) applied to a US/other counterparty, or an out-of-state US governing law (Virginia/Arizona/Nevada/Wisconsin/Tennessee/Georgia) on US paper; counterparty home jurisdiction accommodated, documented but undesirable.

walk_away_triggers: No governing law and no dispute-resolution/forum clause at all; leaves applicable law and enforcement entirely uncertain.
Governing law specified but NO forum or dispute mechanism; insist on adding a clear court or arbitration forum.

Wholly foreign, non-home legal regime with foreign-seat litigation/arbitration giving counterparty home-court advantage, such as German law/Berlin, Swiss law/ICC Zurich, Korean law/KCAB or ICC Seoul, Austrian/VIAC, or Netherlands/Amsterdam; refuse or escalate.
Ambiguous choice-of-law language such as 'internal laws of the United States'; require a named state's law.

Mixed/inconsistent templates: a Delaware-governed contract embedding operative Singapore statutory definitions (e.g., personal data protection, companies act, electronic transactions statute) with no conflicts/carve-out clause; fix before signing.
Venue fixed at the counterparty's principal place of business/home domicile with exclusive jurisdiction and consent to personal jurisdiction; refuse a one-sided home-forum lock.
ICC arbitration for a low-value NDA dispute (disproportionate cost) where SIAC or AAA was available.
